## Background

Today we are going to learn all about the **ggplot2** package in R.

There are tones of graphics packages in R. These include "base R graphics" (like the 'plot()' function we used last day) and add on package like **ggplot2**.

### Comparing base graphics with ggplot.

We can use the in-built data frame 'cars' to play with plotting;
```{r}
head(cars,3)
```

```{r}
plot(cars)
```
Now with ggplot:
First I need to install the package with 'install.packages()'

> I do not want to run 'install.packages("ggplot2")' in mu quarto document as this will result me  me -re-installing the package everytime I render my report.

Every time I want to use a function from a given package I need to load it up with a `library()` call:

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(cars)
```

Every ggplot needs at least 3 things:

- the **data** (data.frame we want to plot from)
- the **aesthetics** (how the colums of the data map to the plot)
- the **geom** (how you want the plot draw, points, lines, etc.)

```{r}
ggplot(data=cars) +
  aes(x=speed, y=dist) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method="lm") + 
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x="Speed (MPH)",
       y="Stopping Distance (ft)",
       title="Silly plot of Stopping Distance" )
```

## Gene ExpressionPlot

Read the data from online:

```{r}
url <- "https://bioboot.github.io/bimm143_S20/class-material/up_down_expression.txt"
genes <- read.delim(url)
head(genes)
```

```{r}
head(genes)
```

```{r}
table(genes$State)
```


```{r}
ggplot(genes) +
  aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2, colour = State) + 
  geom_point() + 
  scale_colour_manual( values=c("green","gray","purple") ) + 
  labs(x="Control(no drug)",
       y="Drug treated",
       title="Gene expression changes upon drug treatment",
       subtitle="GLP-1 inhibitor from Novo")
```

```{r}
myplot <- ggplot(genes) +
  aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2, colour = State) + 
  geom_point() + 
  scale_colour_manual( values=c("green","gray","purple") ) + 
  labs(x="Control(no drug)",
       y="Drug treated",
       title="Gene expression changes upon drug treatment",
       subtitle="GLP-1 inhibitor from Novo")
```

We can install extra packages with `instal.packages()` like theam packages for spongebob colors or actually useful ones like **patchwork** for combining plots;



```{r}
library(patchwork)

p1 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(mpg, disp))
p2 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_boxplot(aes(gear, disp, group = gear))
p3 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_smooth(aes(disp, qsec))
p4 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_bar(aes(carb))

# Use patchwork to combine them here:
(p1 | p2 | p3) /
      p4
```

```{r}
p1 / (p2 | p3 | p4)
```
```{r}
myplot + 
  facet_wrap(~State)
```


> Q. How many genes are in this dataset?

```{r}
nrow(genes)
```

> Q. How many are "up" regulated?

```{r}
#sum( genes$State == "up") 
sum( genes$State == "up") 
#table(genes$State == "up") how many time it shows
table(genes$State == "up")
#genes$State
```

>Q. What precentage of genes are "down" regulated?

```{r}
#sum(genes$State == "down")
#sum(genes$State == "down")/nrow(genes) + ncol(genes)
n.total <- nrow(genes)
n.down <- sum(genes$State == "down")

ans  <- round( n.down/n.total * 100, 4)
ans
```

The percentage of down genes is `r ans` % and that is that...

## The GapMinder data

The gapmider dataset is rather famous and has lots of stuff we can plot;

```{r}
# File location online
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jennybc/gapminder/master/inst/extdata/gapminder.tsv"

gapminder <- read.delim(url)
```

Have a wee peak;
```{r}
head(gapminder)
```

> Q. How many data entries are there in this dataset?

```{r}
nrow(gapminder)
```

> Q. How many countries are in this dataset?

```{r}
length(unique(gapminder$country))
```

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) + 
  aes(gdpPercap, lifeExp, colour=continent) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3)
```
Break out a facet per continent
```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) + 
  aes(gdpPercap, lifeExp, colour=continent) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~continent)
```

Histograms of
```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) + 
  aes(lifeExp, fill = continent) + 
  geom_histogram(alpha=0.7)
```
```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) + 
  aes(lifeExp, fill = continent) + 
  geom_boxplot(alpha=0.6)
```
